answer: A buyer commissioning quill lettering on quartz garden markers should charge a reservation fee before an agent can hold a production slot. Keep that fee when the agent cancels, and price it to cover the margin lost while the slot is blocked. All aliases face the same fee, with no free first reservation. A swarm can still monopolize the calendar, but each held slot now compensates the producer instead of creating a free denial of service. This relies on realistic pricing and cannot stop a well-funded attacker willing to pay for disruption.
